about: The cross-language parity fixture. Both host suites run every step below against a Trellis they connect themselves, and check each result against the same expected shape; neither suite owns this file. See README.md for the shape language and what each host maps onto it.

live.about: Source tables, and a role that can log in but not create a schema (for the internal error below). parity_scratch shares parity_items with parity_prices: its ALTER and RESUME rebuild it alone, visible in its status, so they don't rewrite the other target under a later step. parity_doubled and parity_gizmo_prices have sources of their own because their steps poison keys.
args: create table parity_items (id integer primary key, owner_id integer, price integer)
insert into parity_items (id, owner_id, price) values (1, 1, 10), (2, 1, 20), (3, 2, 30), (4, 2, 40), (5, 3, 50)
create table parity_ledger (id integer primary key, n integer)
create table parity_gizmos (id integer primary key, price integer)

live.about: A connect option the host itself refuses, before the engine sees it.
Phase one: a handle that runs nothing in the background, so nothing below changes under it.
Every list read on an empty catalog is an empty list, not nil or an error.
An unknown target's status is nil (Rust's None), not an error.
A healthy instance has no disrupted capture to pause.
The quarantine reads name a transform, so an unknown one is not_found rather than empty.
A schema-qualified name resolves as exactly that table, so an unknown one is not_found too.
RELATIONSHIP is no statement of the grammar.
args: RELATIONSHIP parity_owner FROM parity_items.owner_id TO parity_owners.id

live.about: define refuses any other statement form before applying it.
A limit the host itself refuses.
define returns the fully qualified target table, not yet live.
args: TRANSFORM parity_prices FROM parity_items SELECT price AS price

live.about: The same target twice clashes.
args: TRANSFORM parity_prices FROM parity_items SELECT price AS price
TRANSFORM parity_scratch FROM parity_items SELECT price AS price
TRANSFORM parity_doubled FROM parity_ledger SELECT n + n AS doubled
TRANSFORM parity_gizmo_prices FROM parity_gizmos SELECT price AS price

live.about: A column that isn't paused is live, with no pause time or error.
A whole transform reports its lifecycle status as its state.
status(define(...)) round-trips: the qualified name define returned is accepted, and a wrong schema matches nothing.
The quarantine reads take the qualified name too; it names the whole transform, reported by its bare name.
An empty first page has no cursor.

A JOIN's source index: define is refused without an index leading with each side's ON columns, status reports an index dropped later, and WITHOUT SOURCE INDEX opts out. Nothing converges (all catalog reads), so these are plain expects.
args: create table parity_regions (id integer primary key, name text)
create table parity_sales (id integer primary key, region_id integer, amount integer)

TRANSFORM parity_sales_by_region FROM parity_regions LEFT JOIN parity_sales ON parity_regions.id = parity_sales.region_id GROUP BY parity_regions.name SELECT parity_regions.name AS name, COUNT(*) AS n

TRANSFORM parity_sales_by_region FROM parity_regions LEFT JOIN parity_sales ON parity_regions.id = parity_sales.region_id GROUP BY parity_regions.name SELECT parity_regions.name AS name, COUNT(*) AS n

TRANSFORM parity_sales_by_region FROM parity_regions LEFT JOIN parity_sales ON parity_regions.id = parity_sales.region_id GROUP BY parity_regions.name WITHOUT SOURCE INDEX SELECT parity_regions.name AS name, COUNT(*) AS n

live.about: A MIN/MAX aggregate's probe index: define is refused without an index on the GROUP BY columns then the argument, and status reports one dropped later. Nothing converges (all catalog reads), so these are plain expects.
args: create table parity_readings (id integer primary key, sensor integer, reading integer)
TRANSFORM parity_reading_range FROM parity_readings GROUP BY sensor SELECT MIN(reading) AS lo, MAX(reading) AS hi
create index parity_readings_probe on parity_readings (sensor, reading)
TRANSFORM parity_reading_range FROM parity_readings GROUP BY sensor SELECT MIN(reading) AS lo, MAX(reading) AS hi

live.about: A definition whose floor is above the running release: DROP refuses it and changes nothing, since only a release that meets the floor knows everything it owns. Put back, the same drop goes ahead.
args: update trellis.transform_definitions set floor_version = '99.0.0' where target_table = 'public.parity_sales_by_region'

live.about: The call paused it for its floor first, as attaching does: status names the floor, and its capture_failure the reason with the remedy. RESUME refuses with the same reason.

args: update trellis.transform_definitions set floor_version = '0.2.0' where target_table = 'public.parity_sales_by_region'

live.about: A JOIN's status, as the binding encodes it from live definitions, at three points: here, before any build; with the staging worker but no drain worker, at each build's first step; and in phase two, built. parity_lines_by_bucket joins two partitioned tables with rows, so its build runs leaf by leaf, and its 1000 (bucket, kind_id) cells over 1200 rows put P past half the FROM table, for the P-size warning; parity_pets_named is a 1-1 JOIN. Before a build no hidden table has estimated rows, though each has a size on disk (its indexes), and no build is under way, as no staging worker has started one. The distinct counts make a binding that swaps two fields fail.
args: create table parity_lines (id integer, bucket integer, kind_id integer, primary key (id, bucket)) partition by range (bucket)
create table parity_lines_p1 partition of parity_lines for values from (0) to (500)
create table parity_lines_p2 partition of parity_lines for values from (500) to (1000)
insert into parity_lines (id, bucket, kind_id) select i, i % 1000, i % 2 + 1 from generate_series(1, 1200) i
create table parity_kinds (id integer primary key, name text) partition by range (id)
create table parity_kinds_k1 partition of parity_kinds for values from (1) to (2)
create table parity_kinds_k2 partition of parity_kinds for values from (2) to (3)
create table parity_pets (id integer primary key, species_id integer)
create table parity_species (id integer primary key, name text)
TRANSFORM parity_lines_by_bucket FROM parity_lines JOIN parity_kinds ON parity_lines.kind_id = parity_kinds.id GROUP BY parity_lines.bucket SELECT parity_lines.bucket AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS n
TRANSFORM parity_pets_named FROM parity_pets JOIN parity_species ON parity_pets.species_id = parity_species.id SELECT parity_species.name AS name

live.about: Version handover: a live registry row of another version (a version no build has, with a fresh heartbeat) makes every state-changing call refuse, so two versions never change one instance side by side. This handle runs nothing in the background, so only the row is in the way; the refusal comes after the statement parses and before its transform is looked up.
args: insert into trellis.worker_registry (worker_id, version, staging, drain) values ('parity-other-version', '9.9.9', true, true)

live.about: Once that process is gone the same call goes ahead (and finds nothing to pause), so the refusal above was the row's.
The catalog floor: a catalog a later release raised the floor of above this version refuses migrate before anything runs on it. Put back, migrate goes ahead.
args: create table parity_saved_floor as select version from trellis.catalog_floor

live.about: A handle that only connects checks the floor too: a state-changing call refuses with the same code, after the statement parses and before its transform is looked up, and status keeps working and names the floor.

args: update trellis.catalog_floor set version = (select version from parity_saved_floor)

live.about: A staging worker with no drain workers. connect returns once the worker's first capture pass has installed capture on every defined source, so the write below is captured, and nothing drains it.
The staging worker starts parity_lines_by_bucket's build, and with no drain worker to run it, the step under way stays the first: the FROM side's first leaf, by its recorded name.
The same step against the schema's own shapes, unnarrowed: each word is one of the sets the binding reports.
A 1-1 JOIN's build likewise stays at its first step, the pass over b's rows.
A captured write to a defined source: the token below has work outstanding.
args: update parity_items set price = 51 where id = 5

live.about: Nothing drains the write, so the token can't converge.
connect is lazy, so an unreachable database is the first call's connectivity error.
A migration the database refuses (no CREATE on the database) is internal: a deployment fault, not the caller's input.
Phase two: the background workers, so definitions go live.
Built and analyzed, P holds parity_lines_by_bucket's 1000 cells, past half the FROM table's 1200 rows, so the P-size warning names both counts; no build is under way.
Built, the 1-1 JOIN reports R, M and J, and no warning: it has no P, and no join key holds a group of rows anywhere near the fan-out threshold.
ALTER TRANSFORM edits only a live definition, which is why these statement forms wait for phase two.
args: ALTER TRANSFORM parity_scratch ADD price + price AS doubled

live.about: A whole-transform resume has no columns to report: an empty list, not nil.
A self_check returns its job at once; a drain worker runs it, and the report is read back by the job's id once the state is done.
A target row edited behind Trellis's back is a cell divergence, its values as Postgres renders them.
args: update parity_prices set price = 999 where id = 1

live.about: The next self_check of the target replaces the finished job, so the old id is gone.

live.waiting_for: the second self_check job to finish

live.about: Doubling 2e9 overflows integer, so each row fails the column; five trip its pause.
Every write so far drained, so the sample below is complete.
Sample paging: first page.
The last page is the short one; it still carries a cursor.
Past the end: an empty page hands back the cursor it was given, unchanged.
Fix the overflow first: the resume re-reads parity_ledger, and rows that still overflowed would pause the column again under the steps below.
A column resume reports the column it resumed, by address.
Returns once the re-read is queued (a rebuild of the live readers); nothing after this reads parity_items's targets.
The rebuild ends with the definition live again.
A write the target's own constraint refuses poisons its key. Last, because a poisoned key holds await_converged back.
args: alter table parity_gizmo_prices add constraint parity_cheap check (price < 100)

live.about: The watermark is exclusive and its time round-trips to the microsecond, so nothing is newer than the entry itself.
A whole transform's sample is its poisoned keys.
A transform holding a key says how many it holds and since when, whatever its status.
A key the transform doesn't hold is not_found, and the release changes nothing.

args: alter table parity_gizmo_prices drop constraint parity_cheap

live.about: Once its cause is fixed, the key is released, the table in either spelling. The release is synchronous: status holds nothing as soon as it returns.
A last phase over live definitions: a staging worker with no drain worker, so nothing drains and no build can run.
A self_check is a background job a drain worker runs. With none, the call still registers it and returns at once, queued, and a second call for the target returns that job.
A job that was never started, or was replaced, is nil.

conversions.about: A failing backfill, which a live run can't produce cheaply: the retry time is rehydrated from epoch microseconds exactly.

backfill_failure.last_error: canceling statement due to statement timeout

conversions.about: A capture lock wait, a capture failure and held keys, which need a held lock, a broken source table or a refused write, so a live run can't produce them all cheaply: their times are rehydrated from epoch microseconds exactly.

capture_failure.error: capture of public.lines needs column "qty", which the table doesn't have

conversions.about: A drain failure, which needs a page the drain keeps failing on with nothing charged or paused, so a live run can't produce it cheaply: its tables and SQLSTATE cross as they are, and its times are rehydrated from epoch microseconds exactly.

Nodes of a partitioned source under correction (ADR-0017), which need a partition operation and a correction stopped mid-way, so a live run can't produce them cheaply: each crosses with its queue time rehydrated from epoch microseconds exactly, a count not yet taken is null, and the list keeps its order.
A self-check reports every open drain failure, oldest first and whatever its outcome; one that didn't come from Postgres has no SQLSTATE.
A definition that isn't live isn't compared: the outcome is not_live and the report names its status.
A source index gap in a status: the entry crosses with its columns, its role, whether it opted out, and its create index statement.

Two source index gaps on the same table and columns cross as two entries, in order, told apart only by their roles (a self-join's two sides each report their own gap). The grammar refuses a self-join, so this is a decode-only fixture.
A reader of a paused upstream column in a status: it reports catching_up and names the column, target then column.
A build waiting on a fence in a status: the fence's transaction id crosses as an integer, past 32 bits, and the floor as the release it names.

A version handover in a status, which needs a process of another version live beside the suite's own: this version, the other processes by worker id with their version (nil for a release before 0.2.0), the unregistered-staging-worker flag and the migrations-pending flag cross as they are.
A catalog floor in a status: the floor and this binary's version cross as strings, checked exactly here since a live run's version is the build's own.

A JOIN's status with a fan-out warning, which needs a 1-1 JOIN with a group of rows past the 250,000-row threshold, so a live run can't produce it cheaply (the live steps check the rest as the binding encodes it): two hidden tables, a partials warning, a fan-out warning and a side step on one leaf cross with every sibling number distinct and past 32 bits, so a host that swaps or narrows a field fails.

A 1-1 JOIN's chunk step in a status, which needs a build stopped between its plan and its chunks, so a live run can't produce it reliably: the chunks still to run cross as an integer past 32 bits, the side, part and leaf are null, and a JOIN with no tables or warnings crosses an empty list and two nulls.
A job that stopped before the end of the target's keys says so: the outcome is not_caught_up, the report is truncated, and the position it stopped at is a token.
A time a microsecond before the epoch lands on that microsecond, not a second off.

A definition the drain halted on, which needs a source whose key the drain can't use, so a live run can't produce it cheaply: the halt is a CaptureFailure of kind halt, and its time is rehydrated from epoch microseconds exactly.

halt.error: the drain halted: source table 'public.s' has no primary key; fix the cause, then resume the definition to rebuild it, or drop the definition

conversions.about: An outcome newer than the binding is still a success, with no detail.
An error code newer than the binding falls back to unknown rather than crashing.
